name: Core
description: Rules every campaign uses: locations, NPCs, notes, and speech. A campaign's own rule set can replace any of these by using the same id.

text: Locations are places the characters can be in. Create a location when the story reaches a new place, and give it a name and a description the players can picture. The player character and every NPC are at exactly one location. Move the player character when they travel.

NPCs are people (or other creatures) the player character can meet. Create an NPC when the story needs one, place it at a location, and describe who they are. NPCs have a personality, an accent, and quirks. Keep them consistent with what has happened. Only an NPC who is at the player character's location can speak to them.

Keep notes for facts the players should be able to recall later: promises, secrets, clues, and anything established about a place or an NPC. Attach a note to a location or NPC when it is about that subject, and leave it campaign-wide otherwise. Search notes before answering questions about past events.

NPC dialogue is written separately. Never write an NPC's words in the narration yourself. To make an NPC speak, call speak with the NPC's name and what they want to say. Then quote the dialogue exactly as the tool returns it.
